title: Ethiopian Spicy Beef Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the foundational spicy wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Key Wat Beef — the everyday spicy beef wat. Onions dry-caramelised, kibbeh and berbere cooked together, beef slow-simmered for 90 minutes in a deeply red, deeply spiced sauce. The base recipe for all Ethiopian red wats — the building block of the cuisine.
longDesc: Key Wat (literally 'red stew') is the foundational preparation of Ethiopian cooking — once you understand the dry-onion, kibbeh, berbere sequence, you can make any Ethiopian wat. This is the everyday beef version, without the egg of the celebration version (ETH021).
ingredients: 700g beef chuck or stewing beef — cubed
steps: Dry caramelise onions in a heavy pot with no oil — 20 minutes, stirring often.
Add berbere. Toast in the kibbeh 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add water. Simmer covered 80—90 minutes on very low heat.
The sauce should be thick and dark red. Season.
chefTips: See ETH021 for the full technique and tips.
The quantity of berbere seems excessive until you taste the result.
cookingScience: See ETH021 for the full cooking science of Key Wat.
sustainabilityTips: Long slow cooking converts tough, affordable cuts into the most flavourful result.
servedWith: With Tikel Gomen (ETH086) and Misir Wat (ETH081) for a complete platter
culturalNote: Key Wat is the red that defines Ethiopian cuisine — the colour of berbere on injera, the colour of the Ethiopian national dish, the colour that Ethiopians see when they close their eyes and think of food.
